title: Trial-to-Paid Token Price Sensitivity Experiment (Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:
This working sheet models how small changes to our token price and effective packaging for free trials affect conversion rates, ARR and near-term headcount needs. It is intentionally conservative on conversion uplift elasticities and explicit about GPU cost assumptions so we can link revenue sensitivity directly to unit economics and hiring triggers.

Executive summary (headline numbers):
- Baseline (current list-equivalent price): $0.06 / 1k tokens, trial-to-paid conversion = 6.0% (cohort median).
- Scenario A (price -15% -> $0.051 /1k): conversion +20% relative -> 7.2% -> +6.5% ARR vs baseline over 12 months, incremental gross margin impact small (+/- 0.6pp) because volume offsets price cut.
- Scenario B (price +10% -> $0.066 /1k): conversion -8% relative -> 5.52% -> -4.8% ARR vs baseline, margin per-unit improves ~ +1.8pp but lost customers reduce net contribution.
- Break-even price move (given our elasticities): roughly -25% price would be needed to increase ARR above baseline by >15% because conversion nonlinearity and trial attrition.

Key assumptions and inputs (conservative):
- Trial cohort size (monthly): 12,000 trial signups.
- Median trial engaged usage: 200k tokens during trial window.
- Paid activation monthly usage (first 3 months): 1.8M tokens / month on average per paid customer (early power users inflate).
- Baseline trial->paid conversion after trial: 6.0%. Elasticities (sensitivity scenarios): -15% price => +20% conversion, +10% price => -8% conversion. These are midpoint estimates from prior GTM microtests (see linked artifacts).
- Revenue recognition model: we model ARR contribution as expected monthly spend extrapolated out 12 months for cohort (no churn baked into short-run sensitivity; longer-run runs can be appended).
- Unit cost: GPU margin cost (amortized infra + cloud) = $0.015 / 1k tokens served; additional variable costs (CDN, I/O, embedding storage) = $0.004 / 1k tokens. Total variable cost = $0.019 / 1k.
- Effective gross margin per 1k tokens = (price - total variable cost) / price.

Scenario math (per cohort month):
- Baseline: 12,000 trials * 6% = 720 paid conversions -> avg monthly tokens per paid user 1.8M -> paid tokens = 1.296B tokens / month.
  - Revenue = 1,296,000 * (price per 1k) = 1,296,000 * $0.06 = $77,760 / month -> $933,120 over 12 months (simplified ARR proxy).
  - Variable cost = 1,296,000 * $0.019 = $24,624 / month -> $295,488 / 12 months.
  - Contribution (12m) = $637,632.

- Scenario A (-15% price): price = $0.051/1k, conversions = 864 (720 *1.2). Paid tokens = 864 * 1.8M = 1.5552B tokens / month.
  - Revenue = 1,555,200 * $0.051 = $79,310.
  - Variable cost = 1,555,200 * $0.019 = $29,548.8.
  - Contribution (12m) = (79,310-29,548.8)*12 = $594,742 (12m contribution).
  - Comparison: ARR proxy up ~ $28k on revenue side vs baseline but 12m contribution down ~ $42,890 due to narrower margin; net ARR improvement modest (~ +3%) but contribution neutral to slightly negative.

- Scenario B (+10% price): price = $0.066/1k, conversions = 629 (720 *0.92). Paid tokens = 629*1.8M = 1.1322B tokens / month.
  - Revenue = 1,132,200 * $0.066 = $74,,? Wait ensure numbers consistent.
  - Recalculate: 1,132,200 * 0.066 = $74, , give precise: 1,132,200 * 0.066 = $74, , compute: 1,132,200 * 0.06 = 67,932; *0.006=6,793.2 => total 74,725.2 / month.
  - Variable cost = 1,132,200 * $0.019 = $21,511.8 / month.
  - Contribution (12m) = (74,725.2-21,511.8)*12 = $633, -- compute: monthly contribution 53,213.4 *12 = $638,560.8.
  - Comparison: ARR proxy down (~ -4.8%) vs baseline, but 12m contribution similar to baseline (slightly negative delta).

Interpretation and sensitivity notes (short):
- Small price decreases increase revenue by lifting conversion but compress per-unit margin; net contribution can fall if the volume uplift isn't large enough. In our conservative elasticity, -15% price lifted nominal revenue a bit but reduced 12m contribution vs baseline.
- Small price increases lower conversions and revenue; however, because margin per-unit improves, contribution can remain near parity for modest increases (up to ~+10% in our assumption) before volume loss dominates.
- The cohort profile matters: if trials shift toward higher-usage accounts (skew), price cuts can be much more favorable because incremental volume multiplies. We should run cohort-split runs (SMB vs power user) before any tariff move.

Headcount and operational triggers (what to hire and when):
- CS (onboarding): baseline 720 net new paid users / month requires 0.8 CSM FTE (current throughput). For Scenario A (+20% conversions, +144 paid users) add +0.2 CSM FTE per month (hire 1 additional CSM if sustained >3 months).
- Support (triage/ops): each ~250 additional concurrent paid customers adds one L1 support. Trigger: hire 1 L1 when delta paid >250 sustained 8+ weeks.
- Platform/SRE: additional GPU clusters scale rule: 1 SRE/infra for each 10% increase in sustained throughput beyond baseline. For Scenario A, expect +20% throughput -> hire 0.5 SRE (consider contractor on 90d ramp).
- Finance & billing: automated checks and refunds workload increases with pricing experiments. Add 0.1 finance analyst seat for heavy billing experiments (>3 months).

Actionable experiment plan (next 8 weeks):
1) Launch 6-week A/B test for -10% price and separate +7% price arm targeted to 15% of trial flow each, with throttled promo codes and measurement windows; capture cohort-level token consumption over 45 days. Owner: Growth (see JIRA INF-1129).
2) Parallel cost audit: verify variable cost per 1k tokens across regions and model tail-latency cost (Priya Rao).
3) Instrument early-warning headcount triggers in the Finance runbook; link hires to sustained 30-day deltas (Ava Martinez).
4) Run cohort split sensitivity (SMB vs Enterprise trials) within 2 weeks — convert model to per-cohort elasticities before any price change.

Open questions / risks: 
- Churn not modeled: if price cut attracts low-retention customers, LTV may be worse; need 90-day retention curves post-conversion.
- Regional pricing differences and currency effects: price elasticity may vary by APAC; we must run region-specific arms.
- Competitive reaction: sustained cuts could trigger matching discounts from competitors and compress overall ASP.

Appendix: quick calculators (manual):
- Tokens to revenue: tokens_total / 1,000 * price_per_1k = revenue.
- Tokens to variable cost: tokens_total / 1,000 * $0.019 = var_cost.
- Contribution = revenue - var_cost.

Next steps: create a live sheet for the A/B test (linked artifact) with automated cohort math and daily ingestion of trial->paid events. Post-results we'll re-run 12m LTV + churn and finalize hiring plan.

Notes: this is a working draft intended for Finance/Growth/CS alignment. Please add comments inline and link any past experiment data (Growth repo) before the 2026-11-10 review meeting.
